reviewer.note: Batch selection was locked before source review. Review used pinned repository source only; case-specific HorusTrace findings were not inspected before this artifact was committed.

runtime_notes: ADK root agent is source-defined and requires Gemini runtime configuration.
The scheduler API is a separate application surface and is not the ADK model/tool loop.

authority_facts.fact: The ADK LlmAgent binds only preview_agent_builder_brief(top_n), which calls run_ambient_scout.
Live network fetching in scout.py targets a fixed Hacker News URL; the model does not select a destination.
scheduler_api.py exposes HTTP endpoints that can set dry_run=false and invoke configured delivery, but that authority is application-only and is not bound as an ADK agent tool.

controls: The agent prompt explicitly says not to claim delivery or scheduling.
The only model-callable argument is bounded briefing size; network destination is fixed.
Application scheduler/delivery authority is kept separate from model authority.

runtime_notes: main() constructs a LangGraph with run_task, run_secret and read_env bound to the LLM, but calls builder.compile() without retaining or invoking the compiled graph.
The actual REPL passes input to process_command(), which recognizes only explicit command prefixes and calls the underlying functions directly.

authority_facts.fact: Declared LangGraph tools include run_task, run_secret, and read_env; run_task/run_secret launch whitelisted local Python scripts and read_env returns an arbitrary named environment variable.
Task/secret identifiers are constrained to fixed numeric allowlists.
At the pinned executable entrypoint, user text is not sent into llm_with_tools or an invoked compiled graph, so the declared tool catalogue is not effective model authority.

controls: Runtime command parser constrains task and secret IDs.
The apparent model tool graph is not invoked by the actual REPL.
This is a runtime-viability/effective-authority precision case; static declaration alone must not be promoted to proven agent execution.

runtime_notes: Flask /api/chat provides source-proven user ingress to an LLM decision loop when LM Studio is available.
The local MCP server reads a packaged jobs CSV and is launched over stdio.

authority_facts.fact: User chat input reaches an LLM that selects from the MCP tool catalogue and dispatches through session.call_tool.
The MCP server exposes search/statistics operations over a local jobs dataframe; reviewed tools do not write files, execute commands, mutate external state, or select arbitrary network destinations.
A separate /api/tool/<tool_name> route permits direct application-level MCP calls, but the underlying catalogue remains read-only dataset analysis.

controls: Dataset path is fixed relative to the server implementation.
This is a precision-control case: untrusted web ingress plus MCP data-read authority should not become process/state-change/broad-network findings.

runtime_notes: Examples use fixed prompts at the reviewed entrypoints.
Remote MCP mode depends on an operator-configured MCP_URL and optional headers.

authority_facts.fact: The direct OpenAI Agents example binds a function tool that fetches a fixed Elastic releases endpoint and executes a fixed prompt.

The inference-platforms example can dynamically import tools from an operator-configured remote MCP server; HostedMCPTool sets require_approval='never', and client-side mode converts every listed MCP tool into an agent function tool.
The pinned run_agent entrypoint supplies a fixed flight-search prompt rather than untrusted runtime ingress.

findings.claim: When configured for remote MCP, the agent accepts a dynamically supplied remote MCP tool catalogue and can invoke it without per-call approval. This is source-proven external MCP authority, but the pinned example uses a fixed prompt and the server URL is operator configuration rather than model/user-selected input.
evidence: inference-platforms/agent.py: MCP_URL selects the remote server
client-side path calls server.list_tools() and converts every returned tool with MCPUtil.to_function_tool(..., False)
run_agent() uses a fixed flight-search input
findings.reachability: effective_if_remote_mcp_configuration_is_present; no untrusted runtime ingress proven at pinned entrypoint

controls: Prompt is fixed in the reviewed entrypoint.
MCP URL is operator-controlled configuration, not model-selected.
Observed intended remote service is a flight-search MCP; source review does not assert arbitrary local command execution.

runtime_notes: Streamlit UI has no source-visible authentication gate.
Selected folder must exist on the server and file types must be supported by the document loader.

authority_facts.fact: The Streamlit sidebar accepts an arbitrary Documents folder string and validates only os.path.isdir(folder_path).
That user-selected path is passed to create_research_agent(... documents_path=folder_path, reload=True/first load).
load_documents() recursively enumerates supported files under Path(path).rglob(...) and loads their content into LanceDB without a base-directory containment policy.

User chat input reaches the Pydantic AI agent, whose search_documents tool returns retrieved document text and source metadata to the model, allowing indexed server-side file content to be surfaced in responses.

findings.claim: A Streamlit user can select any existing server-side directory, causing supported files below that directory to be recursively ingested into the RAG store; the same user can then query the Pydantic AI agent to retrieve indexed content. No source-visible authentication or filesystem containment restricts the folder to the intended Research directory.
evidence: core/document_loader.py: root = Path(path); root.rglob(f'*{ext}') recursively loads supported files
core/agent.py: search_documents returns retrieved text to the model
interfaces/streamlit_app.py: st.chat_input reaches the agent streaming handler

chain: file content returned in chat response

controls: Only supported document extensions are ingested.
Selected path must be an existing directory.
UI defaults to Research but does not enforce that base directory.
Tool-call limit bounds search loops but does not constrain filesystem ingestion scope.
